Saatvik Cleantech | website = {{URL|https://saatvikgroup.com}} }} '''Saatvik Green Energy''' is an Indian [[renewable energy]] company, headquartered in [[Gurgaon]], [[Haryana]], India. Founded in 2015, the company is primarily engaged in manufacturing [[solar photovoltaic]] (PV) modules and providing [[engineering, procurement, and construction]] (EPC) services for solar power plants. As of 2025, it operates three manufacturing facilities in [[Ambala]], Haryana, with a production capacity of about 3.8 GW.{{cite news |last1=Sengupta |first1=Rajarshi |title=Saatvik Solar's 'Made-In-India' Product Offerings At REI 2024 |url=https://taiyangnews.info/videos/saatvik-solar-rei-2024-solar-pump-topcon-module |publisher=TaiyangNews |date=October 28, 2024}}{{cite news |last1=Srivastava |first1=Vikas |title=Saatvik Green To Spend Rs 2,000 Crore On Solar Cell, Panel Capacity |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/saatvik-green-to-spend-rs-2000-crore-on-solar-cell-panel-capacity |publisher=[[NDTV Profit]] |date=November 14, 2024}} The company operates wholly-owned subsidiaries, Saatvik Solar, which manufactures solar equipment, and Saatvik EPC, which manages the engineering, procurement, and construction business.{{cite news |last1=Choudhary |first1=Sanjeev |title=Saatvik Solar seeks Rs 1,000 crore PE funding for expansion |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/saatvik-solar-seeks-rs-1000-crore-pe-funding-for-expansion/articleshow/113700414.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=September 26, 2024}} == History == Founded in 2015, the company began its operations in 2016 with an installed capacity of 125 MW.{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy Marks 10 Years In India’s Solar Sector |url=https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/saatvik-green-energy-marks-10-years-in-indias-solar-sector |publisher=Saur Energy |date=May 29, 2025}} It received a 141.76 MW solar module order from [[Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited|BHEL]] in 2021 for the Raghanesda Ultra Mega Solar Park project in Gujarat.{{cite news |last1=Bhambhani |first1=Anu |title=Saatvik Green bags BHEL module contract |url=https://taiyangnews.info/markets/india-pv-news-snippets-jmk-gail-cil-mnre-saatvik |publisher=TaiyangNews |date=July 2, 2021}} In 2022, Saatvik Green Energy supplied 62 MW of solar modules for the 100 MW floating solar project at [[NTPC Limited|NTPC]]'s Ramagundam Thermal Power Plant in [[Telangana]].{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Uma |title=Saatvik supplies modules for NTPC’s Ramagundam floating solar project |url=https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2022/07/07/saatvik-supplies-modules-for-ntpcs-ramagundam-floating-solar-project/ |publisher=PV Magazine |date=July 7, 2022}} In April 2023, the company established a subsidiary in [[Texas]] to sell its solar PV modules in the American market.{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Uma |title=Saatvik establishes US subsidiary |url=https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2023/04/13/saatvik-establishes-us-subsidiary/ |publisher=PV Magazine |date=April 13, 2023}} Between the fiscal year 2023-24 and February 2025, the company expanded its production capacity from 564 MW to 3.7 GW. In February 2024, it commissioned a 12 MW rooftop solar project at [[Jindal Steel and Power]]'s facility in [[Angul]], [[Odisha]], which has been reported as Asia's largest single-rooftop plant.{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Uma |title=Saatvik Solar commissions ‘Asia’s largest’ single-rooftop solar project |url=https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2024/02/28/saatvik-solar-commissions-asias-largest-single-rooftop-solar-project/ |publisher=PV Magazine |date=February 28, 2024}} In September 2024, Saatvik Solar delivered 70.2 MW of solar modules to [[Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam]] for its renewable energy project in [[Punjab]].{{cite news |last1=Kumar |first1=Deepak |title=सात्विक सोलर ने की एसजेवीएन को 70.2 मेगावाट के सौर मॉड्यूल की आपूर्ति |url=https://www.livehindustan.com/business/renewable-energy-sector-firm-sjvn-deal-with-saatvik-solar-delivers-solar-modules-201726152033939.html |publisher=[[Live Hindustan]] |date=September 12, 2024 |language=hi}} In October 2024, the company secured a ₹302 crore contract from [[Maharashtra State Power Generation Company]] to supply 200 MW of its N-TOPCon 580 Wp modules.{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Uma |title=Saatvik Solar secures INR 302 crore contract to supply PV modules to MAHAGENCO |url=https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2024/10/14/saatvik-solar-secures-inr-302-crore-contract-to-supply-pv-modules-to-mahagenco/ |publisher=PV Magazine |date=October 14, 2024}} Later that month, Saatvik Solar received another order to supply 213 MW of its 545 Wp Mono PERC Bifacial Modules to [[Larsen & Toubro]] for a battery energy storage system (BESS) project in [[Bihar]].{{cite news |title=Saatvik Solar secures 213MW solar PV modules supply contract from L&T Energy |url=https://www.manufacturingtodayindia.com/saatvik-solar-secures-213mw-solar-pv-modules-supply-contract-from-lt-energy |publisher=Manufacturing Today |date=October 10, 2024}} In November 2024, Saatvik Green Energy partnered with [[Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited]] to supply solar-powered [[Submersible pump|submersible pumps]] across 250 sites in [[Maharashtra]] to enhance water access for irrigation and other purposes.{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy enters solar pump biz with order from Maharashtra |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/saatvik-green-energy-enters-solar-pump-biz-with-order-from-maharashtra/article68864109.ece |publisher=[[The Hindu Business Line]] |date=November 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241114031515/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/saatvik-green-energy-enters-solar-pump-biz-with-order-from-maharashtra/article68864109.ece |archive-date=November 14, 2024}}{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy partners with MSEDCL to supply solar pumps in Maharashtra |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/saatvik-green-energy-partners-with-msedcl-to-supply-solar-pumps-in-maharashtra/115276752 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=November 14, 2024}} In January 2025, Saatvik Green Energy was awarded two solar Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contracts by Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL) for a combined capacity of 23 MW. The projects comprised an 11 MW solar plant at Lamlehri, using mono-PERC technology, and a 12 MW plant at Gondpur Bulla, using N-TOPCon technology. The Lamlehri project generates an estimated 17.13 million units of green energy annually, while the Gondpur plant produces about 19.13 million units per year.{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy bags 23 MW solar projects from Himachal govt |url=https://manufacturing.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/energy/saatvik-green-energy-bags-23-mw-solar-projects-from-himachal-govt/117487931 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=January 23, 2025}} Also in January 2025, the company signed a supply agreement valued at more than ₹1,500 crore for 1 GW of N-TOPCon solar PV modules with a domestic energy producer.{{cite news |last1=Anand |first1=Saurav |title=Saatvik Green Energy secures ₹1,500 crore solar module contract |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/saatvik-green-energy-secures-1500-crore-solar-module-contract/117076261 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=January 9, 2025}} In August 2025, Saatvik Solar was added to the [[Ministry of New and Renewable Energy]]'s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) with a listed capacity of 1,941 MW.{{cite news |title=Solar Module Capacity Under ALMM Grows by 8.8 GW |url=https://www.mercomindia.com/solar-module-capacity-under-almm-grows-by-8-8-gw |publisher=Mercom India |date=August 14, 2015}} In October 2025, the company secured solar module orders worth ₹488 crore, while its subsidiary, Saatvik Solar Industries, received a separate order of ₹219.6 crore.{{cite news |last1=Rani |first1=Megha |title=Saatvik Green Energy bags ₹488 crore solar module orders |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/saatvik-green-energy-bags-rs-488-crore-solar-module-orders-19706415.htm |publisher=[[CNBC TV18]] |date=October 7, 2025}} The company inducted cricketer [[Ravindra Jadeja]] as its brand ambassador in 2023{{cite news |title=Saatvik Solar ropes in Ravindra Jadeja as brand ambassador |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/brandwagon-saatvik-solar-ropes-in-ravindra-jadeja-as-brand-ambassador-3232420/ |publisher=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]] |date=September 4, 2023}} and actor [[Kartik Aaryan]]{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy unveils new TVC featuring Brand Ambassador Kartik Aaryan |url=https://www.medianews4u.com/saatvik-green-energy-unveils-new-tvc-featuring-brand-ambassador-kartik-aaryan/ |publisher=Medianews4u |date=August 2, 2025}} in 2025. Under the [[Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Yojana|PM-Kusum Scheme]], the company was awarded a project by [[Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited]] in September 2025 to install 1,500 solar water pumps across various districts in Maharashtra.{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy bags solar pumps order in Maharashtra |url=https://manufacturing.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/energy/saatvik-green-energy-bags-solar-pumps-order-in-maharashtra/123646062 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=September 2, 2025}} == Operations == The company's operations are centered around its three manufacturing facilities in Ambala, [[Haryana]], with a combined production capacity of 3.8 GW. A new integrated manufacturing facility is under development in the [[Ganjam district]] of [[Odisha]], with an investment of ₹2,000 crore planned for Phase-1.{{cite news |last1=Nair |first1=Avinash |title=As incentives soar, solar PV manufacturers strategically choose states |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/as-incentives-soar-solar-pv-manufacturers-strategically-choose-states/article68772254.ece |publisher=[[The Hindu Business Line]] |date=October 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241019102157/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/as-incentives-soar-solar-pv-manufacturers-strategically-choose-states/article68772254.ece#selection-1963.0-1963.12 |archive-date=October 19, 2024}} It is designed to have a production capacity of 4.8 GW for solar cells and 4 GW for modules.{{cite news |last1=Ojha |first1=Shreeyashi |title=Saatvik Solar to build 4.8GW solar cell, 4GW module facility in Odisha, India |url=https://www.pv-tech.org/saatvik-solar-4-8gw-solar-cell-4gw-module-manufacturing-india/ |publisher=PV Tech |date=June 9, 2025}}{{cite news |last1=Nair |first1=Avinash |title=As incentives soar, solar PV manufacturers strategically choose states |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/as-incentives-soar-solar-pv-manufacturers-strategically-choose-states/article68772254.ece |publisher=[[The Hindu Business Line]] |date=October 19, 2024}} Its solar EPC division has an installed capacity of 69.12 MW. Saatvik Green Energy manufactures solar photovoltaic modules using both mono-PERC and N-TOPCon technologies. The company's product range includes modules with power ratings of up to 580 Wp. Its modules incorporate designs such as half-cut cells and multi-busbar configurations, which are used to improve module efficiency and reduce energy losses. The company supplies solar modules for utility, commercial, and residential projects, and also undertakes engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contracts. It has supplied solar PV modules for various large-scale projects, including the [[Government of India]]'s [[Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Yojana|PM-KUSUM Yojana]]. Its notable clients include [[Maharashtra State Power Generation Company]], [[Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited]], and Avaada. In June 2024, the company was recognized as a "Top Performer" in the PV Module Reliability Scorecard by Kiwa PVEL for its high-efficiency mono-bifacial half-cut PV modules.{{cite news |last1=Dhiman |first1=Akash |title=Saatvik Solar Secures Position As Kiwa PVEL Top Performer |url=https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/saatvik-solar-secures-position-as-kiwa-pvel-top-performer |publisher=Saur Energy |date=June 11, 2024}} Some of its notable projects include supplying solar modules for the 61.42 MW floating solar power project at [[Ramagundam]], [[Telangana]]; the 72.15 MW Raghanseda Solar Park in the [[Banaskantha district]], Gujarat; and the 70.2 MW project for SJVN Green Energy in [[Punjab]].{{cite news |last1=Sinha |first1=Ritwik |title=Saatvik: Solar play |url=https://businessindia.co/magazine/corporate-report/saatvik-solar-play |publisher=[[Business India]] |date=September 3, 2025}} == Financials == During the financial year 2024–25, Saatvik Green Energy reported a revenue of ₹2,192.5 crore, an [[EBITDA]] of ₹353.9 crore, and a net profit of ₹213.9 crore.{{cite web |title=Saatvik Green Energy IPO |url=https://www.jmfinancialservices.in/blogs-and-articles/saatvik-green-energy-ipo |publisher=[[JM Financial]] |date=September 18, 2025}} In the previous financial year 2023–24, the company recorded a revenue of ₹1,097 crore and a net profit of ₹100.47 crore. The company had filed a draft prospectus with [[SEBI]] in November 2024 for an [[initial public offering]] (IPO). It got listed on 26 September 2025 on both the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] (BSE) and the [[National Stock Exchange of India]] (NSE). The shares opened at ₹460 on the BSE, slightly below the issue price of ₹465, and listed flat on the NSE. The company's ₹900 crore initial public offering, comprising a fresh issue of ₹700 crore and an offer for sale of ₹200 crore, was subscribed 6.57 times during the issue period from 19 to 23 September 2025.{{cite news |last1=Goel |first1=Saloni |title=Saatvik Green Energy IPO booked over 6.5 times as of third and final day |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/healthcare-sector-q2-results-preview-choice-broking-expects-strong-earnings-recommends-5-stocks-to-buy-11759909682123.html |publisher=[[Livemint]] |date=September 23, 2025}} Prior to the IPO, in September 2025, it raised ₹269.4 crore from anchor investors, including HDFC Mutual Fund, [[Nippon Life|Nippon Life India]], Bandhan Mutual Fund, [[SBI General Insurance]], and [[360 One WAM|360 ONE]].{{cite news |title=Saatvik Green Energy mops up over Rs 269 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 900-crore IPO |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/ipo/saatvik-green-energy-mops-up-over-rs-269-crore-via-anchor-book-ahead-of-rs-900-crore-ipo-13558211.html |publisher=[[Moneycontrol]] |date=September 18, 2025}} == See also == {{Portal box|Companies|Energy}} * [[Solar power in India]] * [[Renewable energy in India]] * [[Solar power in India]] * [[Solar Energy Corporation of India]] ==References== {{Reflist}} {{SPIN}} {{Energy in India}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Renewable energy in India]] [[Category:Solar energy companies of India]] [[Category:Solar power in India| ]] [[Category:Energy in Haryana]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 2015]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
